{

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Client-side max file size hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings",
      "body": "Both validateUploadedFile (line 182) and displayErrorForUpload (line 246) now use a hardcoded 10MB value instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This means administrators' configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb are no longer enforced on the client. Users may be allowed to attempt uploads that the server will reject, or conversely be blocked from uploading images that the new server-side downsize feature would otherwise accept. The error message also shows 10MB regardless of the actual setting."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Animated GIFs are flattened during automatic downsizing",
      "body": "The call to OptimizedImage.downsize passes tempfile.path as the source. This path does not end in .GIF (it is a system tempfile with no extension), so the animated detection in OptimizedImage.optimize (`from =~ /\\.GIF$/i`) never triggers. As a result, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, the non-animated downsize instructions are used, which read only the first frame (`#{from}[0]`) and produce a static image. Any animated GIF exceeding max_image_size_kb will be permanently converted to a still image, causing data loss."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "In-place downsizing does not verify convergence and may leave stale file",
      "body": "The while loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, \"80%\") without checking its return value or confirming that the file size actually decreased. If the conversion fails (e.g., ImageMagick error, unsupported format), the loop runs up to 5 times and then proceeds with a possibly corrupted or still-oversized file. Additionally, because the Tempfile object remains open while the file is overwritten at the same path, the open file descriptor may continue to reference the old inode, so Upload.create_for may read the original oversized file instead of the downsized version. The tempfile should be closed and reopened, or the output written to a separate path and atomically replaced."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 55,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "URL download size limit ignores per-type settings",
      "body": "The change from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes applies to all URL-based uploads, including attachments (type != 'image'). While Upload.create_for may later reject non-images based on max_attachment_size_kb, this allows a download of up to 10MB regardless of configured limits and may consume excessive memory/disk before rejection. The previous behavior was also incorrect for attachments, but the new hardcoded value is not configurable and can be much higher than intended limits."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
      "line": 149,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "New downsize method overrides existing 4-argument signature, breaking callers",
      "body": "The addition of `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely overrides the earlier method at line 145 which accepted `max_width`, `max_height`. Any existing code or plugin that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now pass four positional arguments into a method expecting three, raising ArgumentError. The old method is dead code and the API has silently changed. If the intention was to support both string dimensions and width/height, a different approach (e.g., splat args or a single dimensions keyword) is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 64,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests for automatic image downsizing",
      "body": "The new downsizing loop has no corresponding test coverage. Scenarios such as successful reduction, failure to reduce below the limit, animated GIF preservation, in-place overwrite consistency, and interaction with max_image_size_kb = 0 are all untested. Given the potential for data loss and file corruption, automated tests are essential before merging."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Client-side max file size hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings
findings.body: Both validateUploadedFile (line 182) and displayErrorForUpload (line 246) now use a hardcoded 10MB value instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This means administrators' configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb are no longer enforced on the client. Users may be allowed to attempt uploads that the server will reject, or conversely be blocked from uploading images that the new server-side downsize feature would otherwise accept. The error message also shows 10MB regardless of the actual setting.

findings.title: Animated GIFs are flattened during automatic downsizing
findings.body: The call to OptimizedImage.downsize passes tempfile.path as the source. This path does not end in .GIF (it is a system tempfile with no extension), so the animated detection in OptimizedImage.optimize (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) never triggers. As a result, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, the non-animated downsize instructions are used, which read only the first frame (`#{from}[0]`) and produce a static image. Any animated GIF exceeding max_image_size_kb will be permanently converted to a still image, causing data loss.

findings.title: In-place downsizing does not verify convergence and may leave stale file
findings.body: The while loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%") without checking its return value or confirming that the file size actually decreased. If the conversion fails (e.g., ImageMagick error, unsupported format), the loop runs up to 5 times and then proceeds with a possibly corrupted or still-oversized file. Additionally, because the Tempfile object remains open while the file is overwritten at the same path, the open file descriptor may continue to reference the old inode, so Upload.create_for may read the original oversized file instead of the downsized version. The tempfile should be closed and reopened, or the output written to a separate path and atomically replaced.

findings.title: URL download size limit ignores per-type settings
findings.body: The change from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes applies to all URL-based uploads, including attachments (type != 'image'). While Upload.create_for may later reject non-images based on max_attachment_size_kb, this allows a download of up to 10MB regardless of configured limits and may consume excessive memory/disk before rejection. The previous behavior was also incorrect for attachments, but the new hardcoded value is not configurable and can be much higher than intended limits.

findings.title: New downsize method overrides existing 4-argument signature, breaking callers
findings.body: The addition of `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely overrides the earlier method at line 145 which accepted `max_width`, `max_height`. Any existing code or plugin that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now pass four positional arguments into a method expecting three, raising ArgumentError. The old method is dead code and the API has silently changed. If the intention was to support both string dimensions and width/height, a different approach (e.g., splat args or a single dimensions keyword) is needed.

findings.title: No tests for automatic image downsizing
findings.body: The new downsizing loop has no corresponding test coverage. Scenarios such as successful reduction, failure to reduce below the limit, animated GIF preservation, in-place overwrite consistency, and interaction with max_image_size_kb = 0 are all untested. Given the potential for data loss and file corruption, automated tests are essential before merging.
